question: In your multi-agent research system, you changed the signature of parse_pdf_section, a helper that the document analysis subagent uses. A teammate ran Grep for parse_pdf_section and updated every match. The wrapper module doc_tools.py imports this helper and exposes several functions of its own, and the report subagent now fails in a file that calls extract_section from doc_tools.py. Which two actions would find the call sites that the first search missed?

options.text: Rerun Grep for parse_pdf_section with case-insensitive matching, because the missed call site probably spells the function name with a different capitalization.
options.reason: The missed callers use the names that the wrapper exports, so any search for the original name alone misses them, whatever the capitalization.

options.text: Use Grep across the whole codebase for each name that doc_tools.py exports, and update every call site that these searches return.
options.reason: After the exported names are known, searching for each name across the codebase finds the callers that reach the helper through the wrapper.

options.text: Update only the file that the runtime error names, because the error trace shows the single call site that the first search missed.
options.reason: One error shows one failure, but other callers can use other exported names; only a search for each exported name finds all of them.

options.text: Read doc_tools.py and list every name that it exports, including extract_section and any other function that calls parse_pdf_section.
options.reason: Tracing usage across a wrapper module starts by identifying all the names that the wrapper exports, because callers use those names and not the original one.

options.text: Use Grep to search only for extract_section, because the error trace shows that this is the name the first search missed.
options.reason: The wrapper exposes several functions, so searching for one exported name skips the step of identifying all exported names and leaves other callers unfound.
